turns.answer:
As of 11 Nov 2026, the latest stable release I can confirm is Node.js 26.13.0. It was published on 28 October 2026 and moved the 26 line ("Lithium") into Long Term Support. Support runs until 30 April 2029.

A security update is due today. The Node.js project said it would release new 26.x, 24.x and 22.x versions on or shortly after 11 November 2026. I couldn't find the new version numbers yet, so check nodejs.org for a newer patch.

For production, use the LTS line. One guide advises nothing older than 26.12.1, which has the 21 October security fixes. Node 27 is only an alpha.

turns.user: Compare the free tiers of Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare Pages for a small side project.
turns.answer:
For a small side project, Cloudflare Pages is the most forgiving, Netlify is the tightest, and Vercel sits in between but is non-commercial only. Figures below are from each vendor's docs, as of 11 Nov 2026.

| | Vercel Hobby | Netlify Free | Cloudflare Pages Free |
|---|---|---|---|
| Traffic/usage | First 100 GB data transfer, 1M function invocations | 300 credits/month, hard limit | Unlimited free requests on purely static projects |
| Builds/deploys | 100 deployments per day | 15 credits per production deploy; previews free | 500 builds/month, 1 at a time |
| Projects | 200 | 500 | 100 per account |
| Commercial use | Not allowed | Allowed (per the 2024 blog on the older free plan) | No restriction found |
| If you exceed | Wait up to 30 days | All projects on your account pause | Workers/Functions: 100,000 requests/day |

**Caveats:**
- Netlify's credit system burns quickly with traffic. Bandwidth costs 20 credits per GB and web requests 2 credits per 10,000, so 300 credits don't stretch far.
- Cloudflare says Workers is the primary platform and new projects should start there.
- Vercel cron jobs on Hobby run at most once per day.

setup.user: Which managed Postgres hosting is cheapest for a small app: Neon, Supabase, or AWS RDS?
setup.answer:
Neon is usually the cheapest for a small app. As of 3 Nov 2026, it has a free tier and paid usage with no monthly minimum.

| | Free | Cheapest paid |
|---|---|---|
| Neon | $0, with 1 GB storage per project | Typical spend is about $15/month for a small database on Launch |
| Supabase | $0 with 500 MB, but projects pause after 1 week of inactivity | $25/month for a single Micro-compute project |
| AWS RDS | New accounts get $100 in credits, plus up to $100 more | Instance-hours plus storage, billed even when idle (no small-instance rate found) |

- **Neon:** Compute suspends when idle and you stop accruing CU-hours, but storage still bills.
- **Supabase:** The $25 includes backups and Auth, and it never pauses.
- **RDS:** It's cheap only while the free credits last. I couldn't confirm a small-instance price, so check the AWS calculator.

The Neon-vs-Supabase worked examples come from Neon's own guide, so they favour Neon.

turns.user: Is GPT-4 still the newest OpenAI model?
turns.answer:
No. As of 11 Nov 2026, GPT-4 is several generations behind.

- **Most capable general model:** GPT-6 Astra is the most capable general-purpose model in the GPT-6 family. It was released on 3 September 2026.
- **Newest general-purpose release:** GPT-6.1 Terra, introduced 26 October, is the newest general-purpose GPT release for Work, Codex, and the API.
- **Newest model overall:** GPT-6 Cyber, OpenAI's cybersecurity model, was announced on 5 November 2026. Access is limited. It's initially only available to a select group of approved Daybreak Red customers.
